```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Patient addresses, customer lists and case files often cannot be sent to an online geocoding
service. gridpin geocodes them on your computer: the address text is matched against a country
file stored locally, and nothing about the addresses goes over the network.

## What goes over the network, and when

Exactly one thing: the country file, downloaded once by `gp_download()`. It is the same file
for everyone, so the download says nothing about your data. You can fetch it in advance, on
another machine, and copy it over; with `GRIDPIN_OFFLINE=1` set, gridpin refuses any download.
Geocoding and reverse geocoding never use the network.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(gridpin)
gp_sheets()          # countries, file sizes, what is already here
gp_download("us")    # once; checked against the release checksums
```

The examples below use `tiny.bin`, a 1 KB file of six made-up addresses that ships with the
package, so they run anywhere. With a real country, pass its code (`"us"`) instead.

```{r}
library(gridpin)
sheet <- system.file("extdata", "tiny.bin", package = "gridpin")
```

## From a file of addresses to coordinates

```{r}
addresses <- data.frame(
  id = 1:4,
  address = c("3 Main Street, Springfield", "10 Oak Avenue, Springfield",
              "Main Street, Shelbyville", "99 Nowhere Road")
)
geocoded <- gp_geocode_df(addresses, "address", sheet)
geocoded[, c("id", "gp_precision", "gp_lat", "gp_lon", "gp_street", "gp_weak")]
```

Every input row stays, in order. An address that is not found keeps `NA` coordinates instead of
a guess, so it can be counted and reviewed.

## How good is each answer

`gp_precision` says what was matched: `house` (the door), `interp` (placed between known
numbers of the same street), `near`, `street` or `city`. `gp_weak` is `TRUE` when the answer
should be checked before use: a town-level answer, a low confidence score, or a fuzzy street
match. `weak` is about certainty, not about level: an exact street match is not weak, but it is
still a street, not a door. When the analysis needs the door, keep answers that are at house
level and not weak, and send the rest to manual review:

```{r}
keep <- geocoded$gp_precision %in% c("house", "interp") & !geocoded$gp_weak
review <- geocoded[!keep, c("id", "address", "gp_precision", "gp_weak")]
review
```

How often each level lands within a given distance depends on the country and on how the
addresses are written; check a sample of your own addresses against points you trust before
relying on a threshold.

## A map with sf

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)}
points <- gp_geocode(addresses$address, sheet, sf = TRUE)
points[, c("query", "precision")]
```

Rows without coordinates become empty points, so the table keeps its length.

## For the methods section

```{r}
gp_version(sheet)
```

Report the package version, the sheet release and, for a real country, the file size; the
release names the exact files, and their checksums are published with it.
